title: Synchronize the managed helper with product updates without an extra user command
hypothesis: Product-update and normal-startup integration can remove the separate helper command and signing-variable step while preserving signer identity, prepare-before-stop ordering and no replay after unknown writes.
measurement: Run full component typecheck/tests, product updater/archive gates, an isolated-HOME real launcher/RPC regression, its single-point negative control, and system codesign against an isolated copy using the existing identity without passing a signing variable. Keep native startup acceptance separate from socket fixtures and preserve failed launch evidence.
result: Component npm test including TypeScript pretest passes 332/332; product regressions pass 56/56. Normal startup updates an old sealed source stamp, preserves JSON-only RPC stdout, and does not update again; version/help do not synchronize. Removing just the launcher synchronization makes the old-stamp assertion fail. System codesign identity reuse, signature verification, sealed source-stamp readback and repeat no-op pass on an isolated copy without changing the daily helper. Socket fixtures cover automatic shutdown without a prompt, failure-before-stop, target mismatch, unknown-write lock retention and no replay. All eight native prebuilt files remain byte-identical. A separate native launch created a process but no socket and later exited; the cause and full native automatic stop/replace/start cycle remain unverified. No agent-task benefit, live-provider result or new GUI capability is claimed. Source integration is complete but not npm-published.
